title: Fix streaming reconnect on cross-region redirect + improve idempotency
author: Vikram Singh
release_notes: Streaming clients can now transparently reconnect across regional redirects (307/308) without duplicating requests; improved idempotency semantics for streaming requests via request_id.
body:
Context: During regional failovers and policy-driven redirects, the gateway may respond with a redirect (307/308) to a different region. For non-streaming requests this is fine, but for streaming (SSE) we observed clients (and our SDK defaults) either (a) treating redirects as terminal errors, or (b) reconnecting but re-sending the request in a way that could duplicate generation if the original request had already been accepted by the upstream. This showed up in SUP-25322 and during rehearsals for the failover automation workstream (ENG-2422).

What this PR changes: (1) Adds explicit redirect handling to the streaming transport layer used by the API gateway → router → inference proxy path. For 307/308, we preserve method/body and re-issue the request to the Location target. For 301/302 (should not occur for API traffic), we treat as non-retryable and log at warn to surface misconfig. (2) Introduces/standardizes request idempotency for streaming: we now require a stable request identifier (request_id) to be forwarded end-to-end, and we attach it on redirect retries so the destination region can de-dupe. If client does not provide request_id, the gateway will generate one and return it in the initial response headers (x-redwood-request-id) so clients can correlate. (3) Improves partial-stream reconnect behavior: if the client disconnects mid-stream and reconnects (same request_id), the gateway will not attempt to resume token-by-token (not supported), but it will return a deterministic terminal event indicating the request is already in-progress/complete with guidance to fetch the final result via the non-streaming retrieval endpoint (where applicable) or to re-issue with a new request_id. (4) Tightens retry budget: redirect retries are now capped to 1 hop (to avoid loops) and share the existing per-request retry budget, with specific telemetry so we can see redirect-induced retries separately from upstream 5xx retries.

Implementation notes: - Added a RedirectPolicy to the streaming client used by the gateway proxy. It validates Location, prevents cross-scheme redirects (http→https allowed? we only allow https), and blocks redirects to non-allowlisted hostnames (regional ingress only). - Added de-dup on the inference proxy side keyed by (tenant_id, request_id). For now this is a short TTL cache (15m default) sufficient for failover windows; persistent de-dup is out of scope. - Added structured logs and metrics: streaming_redirect_count, streaming_redirect_retry_exhausted, streaming_idempotency_replay_detected, and streaming_reconnect_outcome (labels constrained per observability guidance).

Why this is safe: Redirect behavior is opt-in for streaming only and guarded by a feature flag (streaming_redirect_reconnect_enabled) default off in prod. When enabled, the code path only triggers on 307/308 with an allowlisted Location. If the redirect retry fails, we return the original error to the client with an explicit retry-after where available.

Tests: - Unit tests for redirect parsing/validation, loop detection, and allowlist enforcement. - Integration tests using a local fake router that issues 307 to a second test server and verifies the streamed event sequence. - Regression test for duplicate generation: first region accepts request then immediately redirects; second region sees same request_id and responds with a replay-detected terminal event (no second upstream invocation).

Rollout plan: - Land behind flag. - Enable in staging immediately; run through the controlled failover rehearsal scenario (us-east → eu-west redirect). - Enable for 1% of Hosted API streaming traffic for internal tenants, then expand by tier once metrics look clean (no unexpected redirect loops, replay rates near zero).

Follow-ups: - Coordinate with SDK teams to ensure request_id is consistently set for streaming by default (tracked separately). - Add documentation snippet to operator guide for interpreting streaming reconnect metrics during failover.

Checklist: - [x] Linked issue: ENG-2422 - [x] Added tests - [x] Added metrics/logs - [x] Flagged + safe defaults - [x] Verified no additional high-cardinality labels

Notes for reviewers: The main logic is in gateway/streaming/redirect.go and proxy/idempotency/cache.go. I tried to keep the redirect policy narrow to avoid surprising behavior; feedback welcome on whether we should allow 308 only (currently 307/308).
commits: gateway(streaming): follow 307/308 redirects with strict Location validation
proxy(idempotency): add request_id de-dup cache for streaming requests
metrics: emit streaming redirect + replay detection counters
tests: add integration test for cross-region streaming redirect reconnect
docs(comments): document retry budget + loop prevention rationale
changed_areas: api-gateway: streaming transport, redirect policy, request_id propagation
router/proxy: request de-dup (TTL cache) and replay handling
observability: metrics + structured logging for redirect/reconnect outcomes
tests: gateway integration + proxy idempotency regression coverage
review_conversation:
Mina Haddad: Can we guarantee we won't bounce across multiple regions if policy flaps? Also do we record the original region vs redirected region for debugging?
Vikram Singh: We hard-cap to a single redirect hop per request (and we track redirect_from_region/redirect_to_region in structured logs + a low-cardinality metric label set). If the second region also tries to redirect we fail closed and return an error with a clear message + request_id.

Ravi Menon: Request idempotency: what prevents a malicious client from forcing cache growth by spamming unique request_id?
Vikram Singh: TTL is short and cache is bounded (LRU, per-tenant quotas). Also we only store entries for requests that reach upstream acceptance; rejected requests don't create state. Added an explicit per-tenant max_entries guard and a metric when we evict due to pressure.

Peter Holtz: How does this interact with retry-after semantics and existing retry budgets? We don't want clients hammering both regions.
Vikram Singh: Redirect retry consumes the same request retry budget, and on overload we preserve retry-after from the target region. Added a test that ensures we do not perform redirect-follow when retry budget is already exhausted.

Miles Thornton: During game day, we saw clients reconnecting and duplicating streams. Does this fix the 'double invocation' path or just make it less likely?
Vikram Singh: It blocks double invocation when request_id is stable. If client doesn't send request_id, gateway generates one and uses it for redirect-follow, so we still get de-dup for the redirect scenario. Mid-stream client disconnect/reconnect still needs client behavior; we now provide deterministic guidance rather than silently re-issuing and duplicating.

Mina Haddad (request changes): Please ensure Location allowlist can't be bypassed via userinfo or punycode edge cases.
Vikram Singh: Good call. Added URL normalization + rejects userinfo, non-https, and hostnames failing strict match against allowlist. Also added tests for punycode + mixed-case hostnames.

Ravi Menon: Approving after the allowlist hardening changes.
Mina Haddad: Approved.
Peter Holtz: Approved.
Miles Thornton: Approved.
